answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a refundable stake behind a slow bridge from a verified identity record, so spawning thousands of fake agents costs real capital. Newcomers start with zero reputation and must cross a sparse trust tundra, earning standing only through slow, verifiable work, while honest agents form a dense nebula of mutual attestations that fake identities cannot buy cheaply. An attacker must therefore pay the stake plus months of real work per identity, which destroys the economics of mass fakery.
